newsitem.title: MACAU: Air Macau to decide on new chief exec next week.
newsitem.headline: Air Macau to decide on new chief exec next week.

text.p: Air Macau, the flag carrier of the Portuguese-administered enclave on China's southern coast, will choose its new chief executive officer next week, the airline's executive committee president Leonel Miranda said on Monday.

"We will decide on the new chief executive officer next week, and there are various candidates," Miranda told Reuters in response to a report that a senior official from China's aviation regulator would become Air Macau's new chief executive.
The South China Morning Post said on Monday that Li Ke Li, an official with the Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC), would take over the post no later than early February.
"Li Ke Li of the international relations department of the CAAC is a strong candidate," Miranda said.
He said the former chief executive, Ng Kian-wah, had left the airline on December 31 after completion of his contract.
Miranda said Air Macau achieved an average load factor of 68 percent last year, which he called "quite good", and carried 665,000 passengers against an initial forecast of 500,000.
Air Macau is 51 percent held by CAAC unit China National Aviation Corp's Air China. It currently flies to Beijing, Shanghai, Xiamen, Bangkok, Taipei and Kaohsiung.
